chunk_findings.detail: `_HOOK_LINE` only treats a hook as failed when the summary has at least three padding dots and the name starts in `[A-Za-z0-9_(\[]`. Pre-commit (and prek copying it) builds that line as `{name}{dots}{Failed}` with a width of about 80 and a padding floor of 0–2 dots, so a failed hook whose display name is longer than ~70 characters, for example 72 `x`s plus `..Failed`, does not match and `parse_precommit` returns `[]`. The same miss happens for a normal short line whose id starts outside that class, such as `-checks................Failed`. Those runs are reported as no findings even though the hook failed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/tool_parsers.py:109

chunk_findings.detail: A version probe that actually starts the binary and exits non-zero is reported as not installed. `probe` returns `ToolProbe(..., installed=False, ...)` whenever `done.ran` and `done.code != 0`. The port in this file defines installed as True, False, or None for could-not-tell, and the reason string itself says the tool is not usable as installed. Given `version_argv` `["gitleaks", "version"]` that runs and exits 2 with stderr `config error`, the result is `installed=False`, which is the same value as `MISSING`/`NOT_FOUND`. Callers that treat False as absent (the companions `is_installed` follow-up) will skip or offer install instead of recording could-not-tell / unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/tools.py:TableTool.probe

chunk_findings.detail: Pin enforcement is cached on the first probe and never repeated for that `TableTool`. `self._probed = self._probed or self.probe()` skips every later `probe()` once a truthy `ToolProbe` exists, including a failed or stale one. Construct a tool with pin `2.0`, first `run()` probes version `2.0.0` and caches it, then replace the binary with `1.0.0` that exits 0 and prints no findings: the next `run()` does not probe, executes `1.0.0`, and returns `CLEAN`. The same cache also freezes a transient probe timeout (`installed is None`) so every later `run()` stays `unavailable` without retrying.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/tools.py:TableTool.run

chunk_findings.detail: `pre-commit` and `prek` only list `finding_codes = [1]`, and the catalog comment says every other exit is `unavailable`, never clean. `pre-commit run` (and a pre-commit-compatible runner) returns 3 when a hook rewrote files and the checks otherwise completed. Given that exit, the run is classified as the tool being unavailable instead of a finished run that modified the tree, so an autofix looks like a missing or broken tool.

data.probe: tools.py probe() maps 'exited nonzero' to installed=False with reason 'Not usable as installed; ask the operator, then run ...' -- a DISTINCT reason from the MISSING/NOT_FOUND 'is not installed' branch (tools.py lines 203-208). The port docstring documents three-valued installed explicitly; a definite 'exited nonzero' answer is False, not None, and the remedy string names the install command. Conscious, not a bug.

data.probe: tools.toml header documents 'any other exit code is unavailable, never clean', and tools.py run() treats an exit code not in clean_codes/finding_codes as unavailable with 'an exit code {id} does not use for a result'. The finding asserts exit 3 = 'files rewritten' with no probe of pre-commit's real exit codes; keeping unknown exits unavailable (never silent/clean) is the documented safe contract given the tool's installed status is unverified.
